entries.snippet: Mississippi's attorney general says a Senatobia officer was justified in using force when he responded to a shoplifting call and fired at a moving vehicle that investigators said was driving toward police, killing a boy who was in the car.

entries.title: A bitter Michigan Senate race rattles Jewish and Muslim voters already on edge over the war in Gaza

entries.snippet: This decision comes as activists and lawmakers argue there are no safe conditions for Ukrainians to return to amid the war with Russia.

entries.title: AP source: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts expected to miss rest of season after blood clots found in lungs and leg

entries.title: Germany: Google must have consent to publish property images
entries.snippet: A court in the western German state of Hesse has said Google is "spying" on people and has no right to publish information about their property on its Maps and Earth sites. The case stems from images taken from the air.

entries.title: North Korean workers treated as 'slaves' at Russian drone factory, says new report
entries.snippet: A new report reveals the plight of North Korean workers at a drone factory in Russia. It also raised concerns that Pyongyang could gain hands-on knowledge of advanced weapons systems through the workers it sends there.

entries.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
entries.snippet: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

entries.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy

entries.title: French authorities impose partial curfews in Paris, Nice
entries.snippet: French authorities imposed curfews in towns and cities on Monday night after cost-of-living and anti-government protests descended into rioting and looting over the weekend. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Germany news: Investment summit draws billions in commitments
entries.snippet: Investors have pledged to pour billions into Germany at a major summit in Berlin, officials say. This comes as Germany agrees to deepen cooperation on AI with US tech giant Nvidia. DW has more.

entries.title: Japan probe sets course for Mars moon
entries.snippet: The MMX spacecraft is on its way to Mars' moon Phobos to collect surface samples that could help answer long-standing questions about the formation of the Solar System.

entries.title: India news: Rubio set to hold talks with S Jaishankar
entries.snippet: Marco Rubio's talks with Indian FM S Jaishankar come as the two countries struggle to finalise a trade deal. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Canada: Alberta rejects separation bid, CBC projects
entries.snippet: Voters have decisively rejected a proposal to begin the legal process toward Alberta's independence, dealing a major blow to a movement driven largely by economic grievances.

entries.title: Australian MP seriously hurt in suspected car attack
entries.snippet: Helen Haines, an independent federal lawmaker, suffered severe injuries in what Australia's prime minister has called a deliberate attack by a man in a car.

entries.title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after 43 years
entries.snippet: Christiane Amanpour's announcement comes after Paramount Skydance's controversial merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, CNN's parent company.

entries.title: Zelenskyy accuses US of delaying Patriot missile shipment
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused the United States of delaying deliveries of air defense missiles already paid for by European allies, as relations between Washington and Kyiv deteriorate.

entries.title: At least four dead after flooding in eastern Spain
entries.snippet: At least four people have died in Spain as torrential rain has battered the country's eastern Mediterranean coast. The severe flooding had left more than 450 people stranded on rooftops, in buildings or in cars.

entries.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
entries.snippet: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

entries.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
entries.snippet: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

entries.title: Kenya: Cult leader guilty of murdering 190 children, 1 adult
entries.snippet: Preacher Paul Mackenzie was accused of encouraging his followers to starve themselves to death. He ran a Christian doomsday cult called the Good News International Church that claimed the end of the world was imminent.

entries.title: Canada: Alberta votes on holding independence referendum
entries.snippet: Canada's oil-rich western province of Alberta is not deemed likely to vote in favor of a real breakaway plebiscite. Nevertheless the separatist movement hopes to gain leverage over Mark Carney's government.

entries.title: Can diplomacy stop another Ethiopia-Eritrea war?
entries.snippet: Ethiopia has installed a new administration in conflict-hit Tigray after federal forces pushed back Tigrayan fighters. But tensions with Eritrea continue to raise fears of a wider regional war.

entries.title: Houthi strike on Yemen government military camp kills at least 50
entries.snippet: The Iran-backed group has claimed responsibility for the attack which killed new recruits at a military camp. The strikes follow deadly attacks over the weekend blamed on Saudi-led forces.
